resources.string: Picture on the big screen. Sound in everyone\'s headphones. Perfectly in step.
MP4 files work best with Chromecast.
Looking for your Chromecast… Make sure the TV is on and this phone is on the same Wi-Fi.
Connect your headphones to this phone first.
Shows what this phone can see. Take a screenshot if Claude asks for one.
If not, tap a button a few times until they do. It is remembered for next time.
On an iPhone or iPad on the same Wi-Fi, open TheatreSync and tap Join.
Chromecast needs Google Play services, which this phone doesn\'t have.
That file can\'t be opened. Try another movie file.
Couldn\'t connect to the TV. Check it\'s switched on.
Connect this phone to the same Wi-Fi as the Chromecast.
The Chromecast couldn\'t play this file. MP4 (H.264 + AAC) files work best.
Use the laptop or phone that started it to pause or stop.
YouTube and mirrored tabs send their sound straight to the TV, so it plays through the room speakers. For headphones in perfect sync, play your own movie files with TheatreSync.
Turn your headphones on and connect them to this phone in Bluetooth settings.
The movie\'s sound will play here.
Allow TheatreSync to see the names of your Bluetooth devices.
Cast a video to the TV
Show your phone on the TV
Paste a link, or share a video to TheatreSync from the YouTube app.
That isn\'t a YouTube video link.
YouTube didn\'t accept the video from TheatreSync. Open it in the YouTube app and tap the cast icon instead.
Tap the cast icon in YouTube and choose your TV. It will show up here under Now casting, with the thumbnail and controls.
In YouTube, tap Share → TheatreSync on any video and it plays on the TV straight away.
YouTube plays its sound through the TV or receiver, not through TheatreSync\'s headphone sync.
Stop the movie first, then cast YouTube.
Show your phone on the TV

1. Tap the button below.
2. Choose your Chromecast in the list.
3. Tap Start now.

Your phone's screen appears on the projector. Come back to TheatreSync to stop.
In Chrome, open the ⋮ menu → Cast… → choose your Chromecast → Cast tab or Cast screen. It shows up in TheatreSync under Now casting.
Android only lets its own settings or the Google Home app start screen mirroring, so TheatreSync opens that for you. Mirrored sound plays through the TV or receiver.
Sorry about that. Send the report so it can be fixed: Send to GitHub opens a ready-made report you submit, or Share it with Claude. Nothing is sent automatically.

The TV couldn\'t reach this phone, so nothing is showing. Make sure the phone and the Chromecast are on the same Wi-Fi network (not a guest network), then stop and start the movie again. Headphones → ⓘ shows the details.
Something went wrong, but TheatreSync kept running. Please try again. Details are in Settings → Crash reports.
Every time TheatreSync closed unexpectedly or caught a problem. Reports stay on this phone until you send them.
Opens a ready-made report on GitHub. Tap Submit there (you need to be signed in).
TheatreSync %1$s · by Quantari Solutions. No data leaves your phone unless you share it.
The TV is playing but the headphone sound didn\'t start. Check the headphones are connected to this phone, then tap pause and play. Details: Headphones → ⓘ.
On · reports go to GitHub automatically
Off · tap to connect GitHub (one time)
Everything here uploads to GitHub automatically. Just tell Claude what you were doing.
Connect once and every crash or problem is uploaded to the TheatreSync GitHub project by itself. You never need to copy or share anything again.
Waiting for you to approve on GitHub…
That didn\'t work. Please try again.
Crash reports and problems upload to GitHub as soon as they happen (or when the app next opens after a crash).
Only crash reports are sent, to your own GitHub project. The approval is stored encrypted on this phone.
Your choice is used for movie sound. To switch which Bluetooth device is connected, use Choose or connect headphones.
Getting the latest from your Chromecast.
Plays two short beeps the same way TheatreSync plays movie sound, and shows where Android sent them.
Did you hear the beeps in your headphones?
Android sent the sound somewhere other than your headphones. Make your headphones the active device below, then test again.
Android sent it to your headphones, but you didn\'t hear it. Check the headphones\' volume, then test again. The details have been recorded.

The TV keeps stopping to load. This video needs about %1$.0f Mbit/s but the Wi-Fi is only getting %2$.0f Mbit/s to the TV. Move the phone closer to the router, or use a smaller video (720p or 1080p at 30 fps).
Couldn\'t prepare this movie for the TV (%1$s). Try another quality.
Converting once on your phone. Next time this movie plays instantly.
Plays straight away, exactly as recorded.
Converted once on your phone for smooth playback on your Chromecast. Lower = loads faster.
Plays on your TV as it is
Your Chromecast can\'t show this video format. Pick 1080p or 720p
Too sharp for your Chromecast (max 1080p). Pick 1080p or 720p
Very large video. 1080p loads faster on Wi-Fi
The TV didn\'t accept the mute. Turn the receiver\'s volume down for now.
Controls the Chromecast\'s volume (room speakers). YouTube sound can\'t go to your headphones.

1. Tap below. GitHub opens with everything filled in. Scroll down, tick \"Enable Device Flow\", then tap \"Create GitHub App\". On the next page tap \"Install App\" → Install on your account → only TheatreSync-.
2. Copy the app\'s Client ID (starts with Iv) from the top of its page and paste it here.
That doesn\'t look like a Client ID. It starts with \"Iv\".
Fixing the sound for your TV… %1$d%%
Only the sound is converted; the picture is kept exactly as it is. Next time this movie plays instantly.
Picture kept as it is. Only the surround sound is turned into stereo for your Chromecast first (usually a minute or two, once).
Your Chromecast can\'t play this surround sound. The TV gets the picture, your headphones get the sound
Tap to turn captions on or off. Press and hold to choose the language.
The TV\'s YouTube didn\'t respond. Try again in a moment.
Older Chromecasts have no remote of their own; these are all the controls they accept. Volume changes the Chromecast\'s own level (your receiver may have its own).
Tap to open the movie player.
No headphones found. Connect them in Bluetooth first.
Android plays movie sound on one Bluetooth headset at a time. Friends listen with TheatreSync on their own phone.
Starts measuring when a movie plays
TheatreSync keeps the headphones locked to the TV automatically. If voices still don\'t match lips, nudge here: minus = sound earlier, plus = later.
Changes only the movie sound in your headphones, never the TV.
Starts instantly: the TV shows the picture and the sound plays in your headphones. Turn on Room speakers too if you also want sound from the TV.

The TV\'s YouTube app plays the sound itself, through the room speakers, so no phone app can send it to your headphones. The headphones you pick here are used for movies from your phone: they switch the moment you tap them.
No app needed. A guest connects their headphones to their own phone, then holds it to the back of this phone, or scans the code. The movie\'s sound plays in their headphones, in step with the TV.
Ready: hold a phone to the back of this one
QR code that opens the TapIn listening page
Headphones with NFC (like the WH-1000XM4): touch them to the back of this phone to connect; TheatreSync offers to switch to them.
TheatreSync TapIn: share the listening page
